prediction.mechanism_under_test: The reranker is pure-numpy and largely serial, so its stage cost should barely move. Retrieval scoring for ALS is the thread-parallel part, so the share should rise slightly (the denominator shrinks) while the exponent, which is fitted on the rerank stage alone, should be close to unchanged.

expected.rerank_stage_exponent: stays within +/- 0.10 of the unpinned O(n^1.21-1.29). The reranker does not use BLAS heavily, so a large shift would mean the exponent was measuring threading rather than problem size.
expected.exposure_parity_flat: remains flat across depth, per-family spread below 0.05. Parity is a property of the allocation, not of the clock, so any movement here would indicate a bug rather than a threading effect.
expected.share_of_serving_cost: rises at the low-depth end relative to unpinned 75.1-99.1 %, because ALS's and popularity's retrieval costs fall when the spin-wait is removed while the reranker's does not.
expected.ndcg_identical: every accuracy figure bit-identical to depth_v2. Pinning must change cost only.

prediction.falsified_if: The fitted exponent moves by more than 0.10, or the 50-to-800 cost ratio moves by more than 20 %. Either would mean §7.6's scaling law was partly a measurement of thread behaviour rather than of the reranker's problem size, and the O(n^1.2-1.3) claim would need restating with that caveat.
prediction.not_predicted: Absolute per-request costs, which fall by construction. Only ratios, exponents and quality metrics are compared across the two conditions.
